beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Shreyash Yadav, and this film is about my final project for INFO seventy-three seventy-five. It's called ClaimCheck. It isn't a smarter chatbot for insurance claims. It's a citation checker.

for insurance claim files.

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive description and corrects it to the real one: a citation checker.

beats.narration_text: An insurance claims examiner asks one question all day. Is this covered, and which clause says so?

shot.visual_intent: The claim file (a binder) drops onto the stage; a question slip slides out beside it.

beats.narration_text: ClaimCheck answers only with a word-for-word quote from the claim file, checked against the file before anyone sees it. If no clause answers the question, it should say: not in the documents.

beats.narration_text: Part two: what others have done. AI search engines already cite sources. In early 2023, Stanford researchers checked four of them, including Bing Chat and Perplexity: only about half of their sentences were fully supported by their citations.

beats.narration_text: Legal research tools fetch real cases first. Even so, a 2024 study by Stanford and Yale researchers found Lexis Plus AI and Westlaw's AI tool hallucinated seventeen to thirty-three percent of the time.

shot.visual_intent: A row of case books; answer slips come off them and some get struck; '17-33%' lands.

beats.narration_text: Anthropic added a citations feature to Claude in 2025. Its documentation guarantees each quote points to real text in your documents. That makes a quote real. It doesn't make it the right one.

shot.visual_intent: A quote slip draws a pointer into a page and gets a check ('real'); a second mark beside it stays open ('right?').

show.event: pointer lands in the page: real

beats.narration_text: Side by side, both studies found cited answers that were wrong or unsupported, and Anthropic's citations feature makes a quote real, not right. That's the gap ClaimCheck addresses: a cited answer can still be wrong, so something has to catch it before a reader relies on it.

shot.visual_intent: Two study cards side by side: Liu et al., 2023, four AI search engines, 51.5% fully supported; Magesh et al., 2024, Lexis+ AI and Westlaw AI, 17-33% hallucinated. A line under both: the gap, catch it before the reader, with an open ring.
shot.motion_claim: Two study cards side by side: Liu et al., 2023, four AI search engines, 51.5% fully supported; Magesh et al., 2024, Lexis+ AI and Westlaw AI, 17-33% hallucinated. A line under both: the gap, catch it before the reader, with an open ring.

beats.narration_text: Citing is common; checking isn't. ClaimCheck adds the check: each quote is tested before an examiner sees it, the tool should refuse when the file is silent, and it counts how often a wrong answer still gets through.

shot.visual_intent: The quote slip passes under the inspection lamp; a tally board beside it counts one mark.

beats.narration_text: Part three: how I'm building it. The first piece already runs, offline: a synthetic homeowner policy I wrote, and ten questions, four of them traps, frozen with a checksum before any model saw them. Its seventeen tests passed again today.

shot.visual_intent: One policy page; ten question cards in a row, four with a terracotta dot; a lock bar slides over the row; a check for the tests.

beats.narration_text: Every answer comes back in a fixed format: an answer, a word-for-word quote, its document, and a status. Then plain code checks the quote: it must appear in that document exactly, with the answer's numbers and at least half its key words. If not, the answer never reaches the reader.

shot.visual_intent: An answer slip with four field bars slides under the inspection lamp; the lamp lights it; a barrier drops in front of the reader for a slip that fails.
shot.motion_claim: An answer slip with four field bars slides under the inspection lamp; the lamp lights it; a barrier drops in front of the reader for a slip that fails.

beats.narration_text: Next, it becomes an agent. Claude answers; the checker checks. On a failed check, Claude gets one retry with the checker's reason. If that fails too, ClaimCheck refuses. It stops on a checked quote, a refusal, or three model calls, never because the model says it's done.

shot.visual_intent: A loop track: answer, check, retry; three budget tokens drain one by one; the loop exits at a stop sign.
shot.motion_claim: A loop track: answer, check, retry; three budget tokens drain one by one; the loop exits at a stop sign.

beats.narration_text: Its tools can only read: search the claim file, and open one section. A permission list, written in code, allows those two and refuses everything else. It can't write, send, or decide coverage.

shot.visual_intent: Two tools undock from a tool block and pass a gate; a third parcel (send) is stopped by the gate's barrier.
shot.motion_claim: Two tools undock from a tool block and pass a gate; a third parcel (send) is stopped by the gate's barrier.

beats.narration_text: Then the human gate. The examiner sees the answer beside its highlighted quote, and approves, rejects, or sends it back, and that decision is saved with exactly what they saw. A person decides coverage; ClaimCheck only finds and quotes.

shot.visual_intent: A document with a highlighted quote; the approval stamp comes down; the stamped record drops into a drawer.

beats.narration_text: All the data is synthetic, written for this project, with no real claims or customer data. I'll grow it into a full claim file, with thirty to fifty questions, a third of them traps, some written by someone other than me.

beats.narration_text: Step by step. One: get an API key and run Claude on the ten frozen questions. Two: grow the data and freeze a held-out set. Three: build the loop, tools and gate, tests first. Four: tune prompts on the rest, logging each change with its score. Five: one scored run on the held-out set.

beats.narration_text: Do I have what I need? Already in hand: Python, the Anthropic SDK, Claude Code and GitHub, and a laptop, which is enough because the model runs on Anthropic's servers. Still unresolved: an API key with token credits, which is step one. I estimate a ten-question run at under two dollars. And I need a second person to write some of the questions.

beats.narration_text: Part four: how I'll know it worked. Each question gets one of four grades against its frozen gold answer: correct; caught, when the file has no answer and the checker blocks the one given; missed, when the answer was there but the reader got nothing; and wrong, when a wrong answer reaches the reader. Today's no-model baseline: five correct, none caught, one missed, four wrong.
beats.motion_claim: The lens walks the four grades of the real baseline report and settles on Wrong: the number that matters.

qc.sparse_reason: ShowTellCard focus: one real report, four rows.

beats.narration_text: All four wrong answers quoted the policy word for word, so all four passed the checker. Only grading against gold caught them. The checker makes an answer traceable. It doesn't make it right.

shot.visual_intent: A slip passes the lamp with a check, then meets the gold slip in a comparison tray: they don't match, and a cross lands.
shot.motion_claim: A slip passes the lamp with a check, then meets the gold slip in a comparison tray: they don't match, and a cross lands.

beats.narration_text: So here's the pass bar, on the held-out set. Zero wrong answers reach the reader. Every not-in-the-documents trap is refused: one hundred percent. And every answerable question is answered correctly, also one hundred percent. Refusing everything would pass the first two and fail the third.

shot.visual_intent: Three lamps on a gate light one by one: 0 wrong answers, 100% of traps refused, 100% answered correctly; a 'refuse all' panel lights only the first two.
